chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj said:

I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about a man who buys a sacrificial animal (Hady), and when he slaughters it, he finds it is a castrated animal that had been previously castrated, and he did not know that the castrated one is not valid for the sacrifice. Is it valid for him, or does he have to repeat it? He said, 'It is not valid for him, unless he has no strength/ability to replace it.'

key_terms.مَجْبُوبٌ: One who has been castrated (specifically referring to the act of castration)
key_terms.يُجْزِي: To be valid/sufficient (for the religious duty)
key_terms.يُعِيدُهُ: To repeat it (perform the sacrifice again)

ai.seo_question: Is a previously castrated animal valid for Hajj sacrifice if the owner didn't know?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the condition of the animal being castrated (majjub) is identified as a defect that generally invalidates the Hady sacrifice. The Imam introduces a crucial nuance of ease (rukhsah): the sacrifice remains valid if the owner lacks the financial or physical capacity to procure a replacement, reflecting the Shia principle of removing hardship in ritual obligations. This ruling highlights the balance between strict ritual purity and practical accessibility in Shia jurisprudence.
